answer: A lasting defense against fake identities is a reputation bond tied to verifiable work: each agent must lock a stake earned through completed tasks before it can trade, so a new identity costs real effort, not just a fresh key. Like timber seasoned slowly, trust builds over time; a cedar planted today cannot pretend to be an old forest. A small, randomly sampled audit fee — call it the saffron check — raises the cost of running many clones at once, because every fake account must pay the stake and risk exposure. An attacker's bill grows with each identity added.
